title: Divakara Dasa. *Jagannatha-charitamrita*, Chapter 3
html:
Jagannatha Dasa Serves Sri Chaitanya; Mahaprabhu Asks about His Former Form

Chapter Three

3.1Listen attentively, kinsfolk, to the deeds of Atibada Gosain.
3.2. Thus some days passed. And that Jagannatha Dasa,
3.3. day by day, with ever-new love, served Sri Chaitanya with devotion.1
3.4. Rising at dawn (?), [he offered Him] full prostration, and gave [Him water] to wash His holy face;
3.5. he cleaned the bed for sleeping (?); [he gave] clay to cleanse the holy hands;
3.6. the tooth-stick for cleaning the teeth; the bath, the rubbing down, drinking water;
3.7. sprinkling the holy body; putting on new cloth;
3.8. the daily duties of sannyasa; cleaning the staff and kamandalu.
3.9. All such tasks — service to Prabhu — were [his] daily duty;
3.10. [also] the darshan of Jagannatha, and the routine of serving [Prabhu] in [His] retinue.
3.11. Seeing this service, Chaitanya put a question to Dasa:
3.12. "O Dasa, seeing your service, We have become very happy at heart.
3.13. About your former divine form — tell Me that story."2
3.14. Hearing this command, Dasa was amazed and rejoiced.
3.15. That (?) Lord is the embodiment of bhakti, the lamp (?) … (??) of the Kali age.3
3.16. "[You are] the Purusha, the Lord of all (?); nothing is hidden from You.

Jagannatha Dasa's Account of His Former Form; Mahaprabhu Calls Him Atibada; the Vaishnavas Murmur

Shloka
3.17. [Skt.] "The hidden (?) supreme abode (?) of Vishnu is the glorious, wondrous Vaikuntha; it spreads out [like] a lotus with its pericarp — this is declared a secret.4
3.18. Above it, on a golden throne, adorned with a jewelled pavilion, in the pericarp is the great abode where Govinda dwells (?), great and imperishable.
3.19. Its southern petal is called the most secret of secrets, the highest. Then [He] entered the rasa on the great throne, which is hard to reach.
3.20. In its midst dwells Krishna, intent on embracing Radha; with one self, with mind and intellect, He manifests (?) the eternal lila."
3.21. "In eternal Vaikuntha, [His] own abode, Bhagavan [was] together … (??) [with Radha].5
3.22. [They] abode as one self, and with great happiness cast a glance [at each other].
3.23. Seeing Radha's face, the Life of the world laughed.6
3.24. That laughter by which crores upon crores of worlds are born in a single moment —
3.25. from that laughter You appeared (lit. "were born"), and You stand in front of the Lord.
3.26. From Radha's laughter I was born, and I stand behind You.
3.27. Looking [at You], [the Lord] gave You the command: 'Becoming incarnate in the mortal world —
3.28. this age of Kali is mighty (?) — perform the kirtan of Hari's Name.'
3.29. You make the unconscious conscious; therefore Your name is Chaitanya.7
3.30. Then Sri Krishna, looking at me, said: 'Be born on earth.8
3.31. You will worship this form, and at the end you will attain that same goal.'
3.32. Therefore, apart from the love of the Couple, my mind finds taste in nothing else."
3.33. Hearing this, Sri Chaitanya became absorbed in meditation (?) on His own abode.9
3.34. Attaining recognition (?) of the former form, the Gosain rejoiced.
3.35. He removed His own wrap (??) from His sacred body with His sacred hand10
3.36. and tied it on Dasa's head, saying: "[You are] very great (ati bada)!
3.37. You have told this most rare account today before Me.

Shloka
3.38. [Skt.] "Hard to attain even for yogis, true, accessible [only] to the Purusha (?)."11
3.39. You have told a very great account; therefore you have become Atibada."
3.40. [Since then] the world calls Dasa "Sri Atibada Jagannatha":
3.41. having heard it from Mahaprabhu's mouth, everyone speaks this word.
3.42. Thus some days passed. Sri Chaitanya in Purushottama
3.43. every day, with an affectionate heart, constantly calls [him] Atibada.
3.44. When [He] called [him] Atibada, the Vaishnavas grieved at heart.12
3.45. Looking at the Odia brahmana, [they] said: "You (?) are Atibada!"
3.46. "Until today we have served, and all of us have fallen to a lower position.
3.47. If we stay with Him, we shall hear nothing but such reproach."
3.48. He indeed is the Lord over all (?); He accomplishes everything [by a mere] word.

Shloka
3.49. [Skt.] "The Maker, the maker of the two makers, the cause of the cause of makers; God is all-pervading — what then can I think of Him?"13
3.50. Such is the glory of the Lord that there is no gainsaying it (?):
3.51. what is done He makes undone, what is not done He does;
3.52. at times He establishes what is done, at times He does not do what is not done;
3.53. at times He delivers great sinners, at times He destroys the pious.
3.54. Since He abides in all bodies, He is called the greatest of all.
3.55. Every day Sri Chaitanya calls [Dasa] by the name Atibada.
3.56. Thus some days passed; the name "Atibada" took hold (?).14
3.57. Unable to bear [it], the devotees went and reported [it] before the Prabhu.

The Vaishnavas Leave for Yajanagara; Mahaprabhu's Letter "More Humble than a Blade of Grass"; the Lord Goes After Them

3.58"You brought an Odia brahmin and called [him] by the title 'Atibada' (?).
3.59. All the servants have become small, [while] his name is 'Atibada'."
3.60. Sri Chaitanya commanded: "Know [this place] as Purushottama.15

Shloka
3.61. [Skt.] 'Even from insects, moths, wood, stones and shells (?) [here] the best (?) on earth is born — what then to speak of a human!'
3.62. The pebbles (?) and stones of this Kshetra, the shells (??) and the wood — regard them thus:
3.63. for other realms they are gods. What then to say of the people!
3.64. Take this into account: the word 'Atibada' is not at all too great for the Dasa.
3.65. As many men and women as there are [here], [all] attain bhakti without sadhana:
3.66. it enters [them] of itself; in other realms this is unattainable."
3.67. Hearing such words from the Prabhu's mouth, all the Vaishnavas were aggrieved.
3.68. They deliberated (?) in their hearts: "It is not proper to stay [here]."
3.69. So they all decided, and cast away their attachment to the Prabhu.
3.70. In despair over the title 'Atibada', they gave up hope of the best of kshetras.
3.71. They left Purushottama and went away, saying: "[We go] to Yajanagara."16
3.72. For six months they stayed there. Thus Chaitanya Gosain,
3.73. together with six Vaishnavas, remained in Purushottama.17
3.74. They worshipped (?) Jagannatha and, [apart from] service, knew nothing else.
3.75. With affection for the host of devotees in His heart, [the Lord] bore compassion for them deep in His heart.
3.76. [There was] a Vaishnava named Haridasa, dearest to all the mahantas.18
3.77. The Merciful One sent him: "Go and bring all the Vaishnavas."
3.78. He wrote a shloka in a letter and gave [it] into Haridasa's hand.

Shloka
3.79. [Skt.] 'Being more humble than a blade of grass, more tolerant than a tree, seeking no honour (?) and giving honour [to others], one should always chant [the name of] Hari.'19
3.80. At the command Haridasa went and entered Yajanagara.
3.81. Paying respects to all, he conveyed (?) [the message] to the assembly in detail.
3.82. With the consent of all the mahantas, he handed over the letter before [them].
3.83. Jagadananda Chakravarti reads out in the assembly the words of the holy mouth:20
3.84. "One should be lower than a blade of grass, endure everything like a tree,
3.85. not rejoice at honour, not grieve at dishonour:
3.86. then a Vaishnava becomes perfect. Where there is division, bhakti does not hold."21
3.87. Hearing this, the Vaishnavas were pleased and said, looking at Haridasa:
3.88. "If He has affection for us, then let Him [Himself] take [us] away from here.
3.89. Without seeing Chaitanya's feet, we shall not go to the best of kshetras again."
3.90. Hearing [this], Haridasa went and told these words to the Prabhu.
3.91. Hearing it, Chaitanya Gosain, looking at the Atibada Dasa,
3.92. said: "Let us go to Yajapura and bring back all the Vaishnavas."22
3.93. Jagannatha Dasa said: "Because of me they have all taken offence.
3.94. How shall I go there? There will be anger in their hearts."
3.95. Hearing this, the Prabhu commanded, uniting [him] with the gods (?):23
3.96. "Our word will stand, [and] between them and you there will be love."
3.97. Together with the six (?) Vaishnavas, the Prabhu went to Yajanagara.
3.98. Arriving in Yajanagara, where the host of Vaishnavas was, He met [them].
3.99. Hearing [of Him], the Vaishnavas were pleased and went out some distance to receive [Him] (?).
3.100. Welcome, greeting, feasting — thus some days passed.
3.101. One day Chaitanya joyfully called [him]: "Atibada Dasa!"
3.102. Hearing the former word, all the Vaishnavas grieved:
3.103. "The very words on account of which [we went] so far — the same reply He has spoken now.
3.104. If we go to Purushottama, we shall hear only these words."24

The Vaishnavas Leave for Vishnupur; Mahaprabhu's Letter about Purushottama; the Gaudiyas Go to Vrindavana

3.105"Let us leave the company of the Odia and go to the land of Gauda," [they] said.
3.106. Looking at Chaitanya, they said: "Truly, [one should] not stay in one kingdom.25
3.107. [Take] bath at Gaya (?), in the Ganga, [at] the sea — make a pilgrimage to the tirthas!"
3.108. Hearing these words, Sri Chaitanya — this is how He spoke:

Shloka
3.109. [Skt.] "Attachment to Krishna, mind on Krishna, wandering (?) along every bank of the Ganga — [yet] in life and at departure [from the body] [My] refuge is the Lord of Nilachala."26
3.110. "My mind, intellect and feeling seek refuge with Jagannatha.
3.111. Whether I live or depart [from this world], apart from Jagannatha I have no other.
3.112. Why then do you grieve at heart? This is Atibada Jagannatha.27
3.113. From My [word] there will be no other release (?): this befits the very great one."
3.114. Hearing these words, the Vaishnavas then left the Prabhu and went away.
3.115. Coming to Bana-Vishnupur, they set up a matha there and stayed [there].28
3.116. The Prabhu graciously returned and remained in Purushottama.
3.117. And at the end of a year all the Vaishnavas, pure in heart,
3.118. because they had no darshan of Purushottama, were dejected (?) at heart.
3.119. They chose (?) one Vaishnava [and] said: "You will tell the Prabhu:
3.120. [we have had] darshan of the holy places and bathing in the holy places."
3.121. Hearing [this], the Vaishnava set out and bowed down to the Prabhu.
3.122. Seeing [him], Sri Chaitanya asked: "Are the chief Vaishnavas well?"
3.123. That Madho Dasa speaks: "By the grace of Your feet,29
3.124. all is well, there is success in all; they practise bhakti to perfection."
3.125. Hearing [this], the Prabhu was joyful: from prema (?) His tears flowed.30
3.126. Thus, after some days, Madho Dasa speaks before [the Prabhu]:
3.127. "The Vaishnavas say: [let Him] make a pilgrimage to the tirthas.
3.128. [You] have stayed in the Odia kingdom, [You] have taken to observing Odia practices."31
3.129. Hearing [this], Sri Chaitanya, lovingly embracing the Vaishnava, said:
3.130. "Madho Dasa, go and tell [them], and give this letter there."

Shloka
3.131. [Skt.] "I have seen the city of Kashi and the Yamuna, beheld (?) the nearness of Madhupuri, seen Gangadvara, many roads (?) … (??) the city of Ayodhya. But in Sri Purushottama — remembering, remembering day and night the world-enchanting form of the Foe of Mura, my mind stays nowhere [else]."32
3.132. That Madho Dasa took the command and gave [the letter] in the assembly of Vaishnavas.
3.133. In it was written thus: "I have seen Kashi,
3.134. Madhupura, the town of cowherds, Vrindavana, the city of Dvaraka,
3.135. Gangadvara, the confluence of the Ganga, Ayodhya, Badarikashrama.
3.136. In these Krishna formerly abode; at the end of the yuga He left them.
3.137. Leaving all the kshetras and tirthas, Jagannatha in Nila-kandara33
3.138. enchants the world by [His] form — therefore I have taken shelter [in Him].
3.139. As long as I live [I shall be] here: I will never leave this [place]."
3.140. Hearing these words, the Vaishnavas all deliberated again:
3.141. "We thought in our hearts: the Son of Shachi, showing mercy,
3.142. will abolish the title 'Atibada', [and] He (?) will take [us] to Purushottama.34
3.143. We shall not go to Purushottama, then! By what shelter would we gain bhakti [there]?
3.144. The former place of Govinda's lila — let us go away to Sri Vrindavana."35
3.145. [Though] this word [is given] in the Vedas and Puranas, they rejected [it — took up] another injunction.
3.146. Whatever customs Purushottama had — those matters they made into another custom.
3.147. They abandoned "Hare Rama Krishna" and began to say "Hare Krishna Rama".36
3.148. They cast away the honouring of nirmalya [and] began to worship (?) the dust of Vrindavana.37

The Gaudiyas in Vrindavana; Rupa and Sanatana at the Gundicha; End of the Chapter

3.149Leaving bathing in the sea, they turned their minds to the waters of the Yamuna;
3.150. leaving the form of Jagannatha, [they turned their] love to Madana-mohana.38
3.151. They cast off the 'Hari-mandira' [tilaka] [and] took to honouring (?) a black (?) tilaka.39
3.152. Leaving the hope of Purushottama, they settled in Vrindavana.
3.153. They cast off acts by rule [and] took to worshipping Krishna by the path of raga.40
3.154. They reasoned in their minds: "Bhagavan is subject to bhakti.
3.155. Since Hari is subject to feeling, He delivers and takes away [one] who thinks [of Him].
3.156. He is pleased by the devotee's feeling (?) [and] for feeling grants the hard-to-attain abode.
3.157. Where devotees dwell — know that [place] as Purushottama."41
3.158. Having reasoned thus in their minds, they took up residence in Vrindavana.
3.159. Circling the kshetra, they wander round the hill of Govardhana,42
3.160. bathe in the Yamuna, [have] darshan of the kadamba tree.
3.161. Thus the glory of the six Gosains became manifest there.43
3.162. Hearing this news, Sri Chaitanya, looking (?) at Mathura Dasa,
3.163. said [to him]: "Take the order, go [and] bring [them]" (?).44
3.164. Mathura Dasa set off and arrived in Vrindavana.
3.165. He told [them] Prabhu's orders. Hearing [them], Rupa [and] Sanatana
3.166. came to the Gundicha-yatra together (?) with twenty companions.
3.167. They saw Chaitanya Gosain pushing the chariot with [His] head.45
3.168. They made full prostrations [to Him], and Prabhu Himself embraced [them].
3.169. Overwhelmed by prema, they did not know their own from others.
3.170. First — Prabhu Nityananda; Sri Sanatana — [full of] joy (?);46
3.171. Sri Rupa Gosain; Sri Raghunatha Dasa — [also] there;
3.172. Sri Jiva Gosain; Sri Gopala Dasa — [also] abiding [with them].
3.173. [These are] the six Vaishnavas of liberation (?). Who will write more of that?
3.174. Having had darshan of Jagannatha, [they] go to Vrindavana.
3.175. Every year they come [and] serve in the Gundicha procession;47
3.176. having completed the darshan of Gundicha, they go again to Vrindavana.
3.177. Sri Chaitanya showed [them] honour, [but] they did not take it to heart.
3.178. Whoever stays near [something great] does not esteem it, though it be great.48
3.179. [Bhrigu], not acknowledging [Him] as Vishnu, struck the Srivatsa with his foot;
3.180. Nanda beat [Krishna], seizing Him by the tuft of hair; the cowherd boys leapt [onto Him].
3.181. [Those who] share the company of the Lord — [such] devotees do not speak of awe (??).49
3.182. Whatever and wherever the devotees speak, there the Lord is found as such.
3.183. With them Sri Chaitanya, saying nothing at all, [remained] silent.
3.184. Offended at the title 'Atibada', they returned (?) [and] went to Vrindavana.50
3.185. But this Sri Chaitanya Gosain remains abiding in Purushottama;
3.186. He chants 'Hare Rama Krishna', bearing love for Sri Jagannatha.51
3.187. Says the brahmin Divakara: "At Chaitanya's feet is my head.
3.188. That Prabhu is the ocean of bhakti: in the boat of bhakti He will carry [us] across."

Thus [ends], in the Sri Jagannathamrita, [the life of] Sri Ati Bada Jagannatha, the third chapter, called 'Anukramani' (?).52

✦

Notes

  1. 3.3–3.10 present Jagannatha Dasa as Mahaprabhu's personal servant. He carries out the Lord's morning routine: the prostration, washing the face, cleaning the bed, clay for the hands, the tooth-stick, the bath and change of cloth, cleaning the sannyasi's staff and kamandalu. He also accompanies the Lord to the darshan of Jagannatha. According to the CC, Mahaprabhu's personal servant in Puri was Govinda, together with Kashishvara (CC, Madhya 10; cf. MP 1.95 and the note to it). Jagannatha Dasa is not mentioned in the CC or CB (cf. the note to VL 9.63). ପ୍ରଭାତୁଁ (prabhātu̐, "from dawn", 3.4) is a tentative reading: the second sign is filled with ink and resembles ଭା/ସ୍ୱ. ମୃତିକା (mṛtikā, 3.5) = mṛttikā, "clay". Karāi … dhaüta (3.4) is understood as "giving [the Lord water] to wash the face". ଗହଣ ଖଟିବା (gahaṇa khaṭibā, 3.10) means "to serve in the retinue, to attend".
  2. The "former divine form" (pūrba dibya aṅga) is apparently a question about who Jagannatha Dasa was in Krishna's eternal pastimes. The answer apparently follows on the next page. Cf. 1.27 and 1.75 (he is a part of Radha) and 1.61, 1.68 (he was born from Radha's laughter). Establishing Jagannatha Dasa's pre-eminence is a running theme of the Atibadi line; for the Gaudiya Vaishnava position see the note to 2.22. Mahaprabhu speaks of Himself as "We" (hoilu̐, 1st pers. pl., 3.12), the honorific plural.
  3. The reading and sense of 3.15 are unclear. The first sign is filled with ink and taken as ସେ, "that". If so, 3.15 is the author's description of Mahaprabhu, and Jagannatha Dasa's speech begins in 3.16 ("nothing is hidden from You"). Another possibility is that Dasa already begins to answer in 3.15. The word ଅଙ୍ଗ (aṅga, "body, limb") is unclear in sense; ଅନ୍ଧ (andha) would be expected: "a lamp for the blind of the Kali age". ପ୍ରଦୀପ (pradīpa, "lamp") is read from the indistinct signs ପ୍ର + ଦୀ + ପ. ସର୍ବଙ୍କ (sarbaṅka, "of all", 3.16): the third sign is smudged. Gaudiya Vaishnavas also worship Mahaprabhu as the Supreme Lord, Krishna Himself (CC, Adi 1–2). The speech continues on the next page.
  4. 3.17–3.20 are eight lines (four shlokas in anushtubh metre) after the mark "Shloka". The supreme abode is described as a lotus: in the pericarp, a golden throne under a jewelled pavilion and Govinda's abode; the southern petal is the most secret; in the centre Krishna, embraced by Radha, manifests the eternal lila. The source has not been found. The imagery is close to Brahma-samhita 5.2–5.5: Gokula is a thousand-petalled lotus, and its pericarp is Krishna's abode. The reading of the first words of 3.17 is uncertain. ବିଷ୍ଣୁ: the first sign is ବ with a lower stroke, as in ବିସ୍ତାରଂ. ଛଦ୍ମ: the first sign is round with a ring below, like ଛ in ପଛରେ (3.26); the OCR gives ବଞ୍ଚ ର୍ଷ. ପରଧାନ: the last sign is ନ, not ମ; taken as para-dhāma, "supreme abode" (or pradhāna, "chief"). ମଦ୍ଭୁତଂ = -m adbhutam. In 3.18 the signs ସ୍ଥ and ୟ look alike (ଗୋବିନ୍ଦସ୍ଥଂ, ମହାବ୍ୟୟଂ); ପ୍ରକାଶୟେତ୍ (3.20) is a tentative reading. As in 1.62, Divakara places Radha and Krishna in Vaikuntha (see the note to 1.62). For Gaudiya Vaishnavas, Goloka-Vrindavana is above Vaikuntha (CC, Adi 5).
  5. Printed ରାବେ (rābe): the first sign is ରା or ଚା with a tail (see the note to 3.17), the second a clear ବେ. No word with this meaning exists. Possibly a misprint for ରାଧେ (rādhe, "with Radha"). ଭାବେ (bhābe, "in bhava") is also possible, but ଭା in the next line (ଭାବରେଣ, 3.22) looks different. The translation follows the context; cf. 1.62–1.63: "Sri Radha and Krishna on one seat… abide in a single bhava".
  6. 3.23–3.30 repeat the account of 1.61–1.75, but here it is put in the mouth of Jagannatha Dasa himself, as in VL 5.113–5.121. Sri Chaitanya appeared from Krishna's laughter (3.24–3.25), Jagannatha Dasa of Radha's laughter (3.26); both are sent to earth (3.27, 3.30). On this Atibadi teaching and the Gaudiya Vaishnava position see the notes to 1.27 and 1.61 and to VL 5.117. For Gaudiya Vaishnavas, Sri Chaitanya is Krishna Himself, who has taken Radha's mood and complexion (CC, Adi 1.5; Adi 4). He descends Himself to give the Name (CC, Adi 3); He is not born of Krishna's laughter. "The Lord" (prabhu) in 3.25 is Krishna. "In front of the Lord… behind You" (3.25–3.26) apparently describes their order in the eternal abode.
  7. An explanation of the name: "You make the unconscious (aceta) conscious (caitanya)". According to CB (Madhya 28), the name "Krishna-Chaitanya" was given to the Lord at His sannyasa by Keshava Bharati: He awakens Krishna consciousness in the world.
  8. Krishna's command to Jagannatha Dasa to be born on earth: cf. 1.75 and the note there (where ତୁହି / ମହୀ also occur). "This form" (ehi swarūpa, 3.31) is apparently the Couple, Radha and Krishna (cf. 3.32). Gaudiya Vaishnavas do not accept the teaching that Jagannatha Dasa is a portion of Radha (note to 1.27).
  9. Printed ଧାନ (dhāna). Taken as dhyāna, "meditation"; the ୍ୟ is not visible. ଧାମରୁ (dhāmaru) literally means "from the abode"; translated "[meditation] on His own abode". ଚିହ୍ନାଙ୍ଗ (cihnāṅga, 3.34; printed ଚି + ହ୍ନ + ା + ଙ୍ଗ) is understood tentatively as "recognition of the form" (cihnā, "recognition", + aṅga). The sense of 3.33–3.34: in meditation Mahaprabhu recognizes His former form and confirms Dasa's account. Cf. 3.16: "for You nothing is hidden".
  10. The word has not been identified. It is printed ପା + େ + a dark sign like ଛ (cf. ପଛରେ, 3.26) + ଡ଼; no ି is visible. Tentatively ପାଛେଡ଼ି (pācheṛi), "wrap, shawl" (cf. Beng. pāchṛā, "cloth"); the rhyme with କାଢ଼ି supports this. The OCR gives ପାଶ୍ମେଡ଼. In the parallel VL 5.122 the Lord ties His uttariya on the Swami's head (see the note there). The episode of the title "Atibada" (3.35–3.41): cf. VL 5.119–5.129. It is absent from CC and CB. See the notes to 1.20 and to VL 5.119.
  11. A single line (half-shloka); the source has not been found. Puruṣa-gocaram is taken as "accessible [only] to the Purusha", i.e. to the Lord; cf. 3.16. It apparently refers to Dasa's account, the secret of his origin. 3.39 is almost word for word VL 5.121 and 5.129: "you have told a very great account; from today you have become Atibada". A pun: atibaṛa kathā, "a very great account", and atibaṛa, "very great".
  12. The "Vaishnavas" (3.44) and the "devotees" (3.57) are apparently Mahaprabhu's companions, the Gaudiyas. In VL 5.124–5.128, by contrast, they follow Svarupa and accept the form of address "Atibada". In Divakara they murmur and complain that they "have fallen to a lower position" (3.46): the author thus stresses Jagannatha Dasa's superiority over the Gaudiyas. Gaudiya Vaishnavas see Mahaprabhu's companions (Svarupa Damodara, Ramananda Raya and others) as His eternal associates, free from envy. A claim to the title "very great" contradicts the Lord's instruction to be "humbler than a blade of grass" (Shikshashtaka 3; CC, Antya 20.21). This is why Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati counts the "ativadi" among the apasampradayas (see the note to 1.27). ତୁହି (tuhi, familiar "you", 3.45) is read as in 1.75; here it apparently carries mockery. Who speaks in 3.48, the Vaishnavas or the author, is unclear. Given the link with 3.49–3.54, these are the author's words on the Lord's sovereignty.
  13. The source of the shloka has not been found. Printed କର୍ତ୍ତ (without ା and ୃ) three times and ଯଥାଦେବ ସ୍ତସ୍ୟ; restored by metre and sense: kartā kartṛ-dvayoḥ kartā… devas tasya kiṁ cintayāmy aham. Who the "two makers" are is unclear (Brahma and Shiva? prakriti and purusha?). 3.50–3.54 are an Odia gloss: the Lord is almighty; He can make the done undone and the undone done. Cf. the well-known phrase kartum akartum anyathā kartuṁ samarthaḥ, "able to do, not to do, and to do otherwise". With this the author apparently justifies the exaltation of Jagannatha Dasa above the Lord's former servants (3.46). ମହିମାଟି (3.50; printed ମହ + ମା + a sign like ଣ୍ଟ) and ତହୁଁକ (printed ତ + ହୁଁ + କ) are tentative readings.
  14. କାଟିଲା (kāṭilā) is understood by the Odia idiom nā̃ kāṭibā, "to make a name, to become renowned". The second sign of the word is indistinct. 3.57 leads into the devotees' complaint; it continues on the next page.
  15. 3.60–3.66 are Mahaprabhu's answer to the complaint: the glory of Purushottama-kshetra (Puri). Even the stones and wood of this Kshetra would be worshipped as gods in other lands, and the people here attain bhakti without sadhana. Hence the title 'Atibada' is not excessive for the Dasa (3.64). The source of the shloka 3.61 has not been found. The readings of the shloka are uncertain. ଶୁକ୍ତିତଃ (śuktitaḥ, 'from shells'): printed ଶୁ + a ligature like କ୍ତି; possibly ଗୁଳ୍ମତଃ, 'from shrubs'. ଶ୍ରେଷ୍ଠୋଽଗ୍ରେ: the avagraha is printed like ୨. In the Odia paraphrase (3.62), ଟେକା (ṭekā, 'pebble, clod') is read from the signs ଟେ and କା printed apart. ଝିଙ୍କର is not identified: perhaps 'shells' (cf. ଝିନୁକ, the śukti of the shloka) or 'crickets' (ଝିଙ୍କାରି, the kīṭa). 'Know as Purushottama' (puruṣottama boli cihna, 3.60) is taken as 'know [the glory of] Purushottama'. Gaudiya Vaishnavas also honour Puri (Nilachala) as a holy dhama. But they see a Vaishnava's greatness in humility, not in a title (see the notes to 3.44 and 3.79).
  16. Yajanagara (3.92: Yajapura) is Jajpur on the Vaitarani river, on the road from Puri to Bengal (cf. the note to VL 6.78). The departure of the offended Vaishnavas from Puri to Yajanagara is also in Madhava (VL 6.59–6.80). There the Gaudiyas are offended because the Prabhu honours Jagannatha Dasa as 'Svami', though he has received no initiation. Here the cause is the title 'Atibada'. This is not in the CC/CB. According to the CC, the Gaudiyas led by Shivananda Sena came to Mahaprabhu every year for the Ratha-yatra and spent the chaturmasya with Him (Madhya 16; Antya 10, 12); see the note to VL 6.65.
  17. 'Six Vaishnavas' (ṣaṛamūrtti baiṣṇaba, lit. 'six forms'; in 3.97 printed ଛତମୂର୍ତ୍ତି, cf. Odia ଛ 'six'). Who they are is not said. Possibly the Prabhu's closest companions who stayed with Him, probably including Jagannatha Dasa (cf. 3.91–3.97). ଭରୁଥାନ୍ତି (3.74) is taken as a misprint for ଭଜୁଥାନ୍ତି, 'worshipped': the second sign is printed as ରୁ.
  18. Which Haridasa is meant is not said. According to the CC, Haridasa Thakura lived in Puri (his disappearance: CC, Antya 11), and Junior Haridasa was among the kirtan singers (CC, Antya 2). In Madhava, Junior Haridasa leaves Puri before the Gaudiyas leave (VL 6.57–6.58). In Madhava the letter to those who left is carried by Shivananda (VL 6.77). The rhyme ଦୟାବନ୍ତ / ଯାଇଁ (3.77) is imperfect.
  19. The third verse of the Shikshashtaka. According to the CC (Adi 17.31; Antya 20.21), Mahaprabhu Himself spoke this verse; the Padyavali of Rupa Gosvami also gives it as the Lord's words. Here Mahaprabhu Himself writes it to the Vaishnavas who left. In this Divakara agrees with the CC and differs from VL 6.75, where the eight shlokas are written by the Svami, Jagannatha Dasa (see the note to VL 6.75). Printed ଅମାନିନ୍ୟେ (ନ with ୍ୟ and େ); we read amāninā, as in the CC. There is a stray stroke above ମା in ମାନଦେନ, and ର୍ତ୍ତ in କୀର୍ତ୍ତନୀୟଃ looks like ର୍ତ୍ତି. 3.84–3.86 are an Odia paraphrase of the verse. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati sees in this verse the foundation of a Vaishnava's conduct. For this very reason, in the Gaudiya Vaishnava view, the claim to the title 'Atibada' ('very great') contradicts the Lord's teaching (see the note to 3.44).
  20. Jagadananda is apparently Jagadananda Pandita, a close companion of Mahaprabhu (CC, Adi 10; Antya 12). The title 'Chakravarti' with his name does not occur in the CC. Śrīmukha ('holy mouth') here is the Lord's letter, His own words. ସନମତେ (3.82) is taken as sammate, 'with the consent'. ବହିଲେ (3.81, lit. 'carried') is taken as 'conveyed'; possibly a misprint for କହିଲେ, 'told'.
  21. Bhedare bhakti na sajāi — 'where there is division (discrimination), bhakti does not hold (is not fitting)'. Apparently a call not to divide Vaishnavas into 'ours' and 'others', Gaudiyas and Odias. The understanding is uncertain.
  22. Mahaprabhu Himself goes after those who left and takes Jagannatha Dasa with Him. Cf. VL 6.71–6.73: there the Prabhu asks the Svami to go with Him, and the Svami refuses. This episode is not in the CC/CB.
  23. The sense of 3.95b is unclear. Literally: 'uniting [him] with the gods' (debatāṅka tule). Perhaps the 'gods' are the Vaishnavas: cf. 3.63, where even the stones of the Kshetra 'are gods for other realms'. Then the Prabhu 'unites' Jagannatha Dasa with the Vaishnavas and promises that His word (the title 'Atibada') will stand and there will be love between them (3.96).
  24. In Yajanagara Mahaprabhu again calls Jagannatha Dasa 'Atibada', and the Vaishnavas grieve again. Continued on the next page. ପାଛୋଟି (3.99, 'going out to receive') is a tentative reading: no ା is visible after ଛ. For the Gaudiya Vaishnava position see the note to 3.44.
  25. In 3.105–3.107 the offended Vaishnavas decide to leave for Gauda (Bengal) and invite Mahaprabhu to come with them on pilgrimage: Gaya, the Ganga, the sea (perhaps Ganga-sagara, the mouth of the Ganga). ସତଏକ (sataeka) is taken as 'truly'. 'Not [stay] in one kingdom' is also possible. ଗୟା (3.107): printed ଗ + a sign like ସ୍ଥୁ (ୟ with a tail, ା merged); the reading is tentative, from the sense. Mahaprabhu's answer (3.109–3.113): He will not leave Jagannatha. According to CC (Madhya 3), Mahaprabhu settled in Puri at the request of His mother Shachi. The Gaudiyas came to Him there every year (see the note to 3.71).
  26. Source of the shloka not found. ଗତିର୍ (gatir): the first sign resembles ସ (ସତିର୍?). The reading follows the chime ratiḥ — matiḥ — gatiḥ. ଜୀବତେ is evidently a misprint for ଜୀବିତେ (jīvite, 'in life'). Gaṅgā-taṭe taṭe means 'on bank after bank', that is, along every bank of the Ganga. The sense: let the heart be devoted to Krishna and the road lead through the holy places of the Ganga — yet Mahaprabhu's refuge in life and at departure [from the body] is Jagannatha. Maraṇe is rendered 'at departure', following the project's usage regarding the Lord. 3.110–3.111 are its Odia paraphrase.
  27. E atibaṛa jagannātha means either 'this is Atibada Jagannatha' or 'this Jagannatha is very great'. There may be a pun: Jagannatha Dasa's name is the same as that of the Lord of Puri. 3.113 is understood tentatively. Literally: 'My release (mocana) is not otherwise; this befits the very great one.' Perhaps the sense is: 'I will not take [My word] back; [the title] befits the very great one.' Mahaprabhu confirms the title again, and the Vaishnavas leave. For the Gaudiya Vaishnava position, see the notes to 3.44 and 3.79.
  28. Bana-Vishnupur ('forest Vishnupur') is evidently Vishnupur (Bishnupur) in West Bengal, the capital of the Malla kings (Mallabhum). Gaudiya Vaishnavism took root there under Srinivasa Acharya and King Vira Hambira, that is, after Mahaprabhu's disappearance. In Divakara the Vaishnavas leave Mahaprabhu a second time, now for Bengal; cf. their first departure to Yajanagara (3.71) and VL 6.59–6.80. There is no such departure in CC/CB.
  29. Madho (Madhava) Dasa is named for the first time in 3.123; he is the Vaishnava sent in 3.119. He is unidentified. CC knows several associates of Mahaprabhu named Madhava, for example the kirtan singer Madhava Ghosha (CC, Adi 10). But the same name does not prove the same person. The rhyme ଚୈତନ୍ୟ / ପ୍ରଧାନ (3.122) is imperfect.
  30. ପ୍ରେମାଶ (?): printed ପ୍ରେ + ମା + a sign resembling ଶ or ଘ. It may be ପ୍ରେମାଶ୍ରୁ ('tears of prema') with the subscripts lost. Then the line repeats 'tears' (aśru jaḷa). The translation follows the sense.
  31. 3.127–3.128 are the Vaishnavas' reproach, conveyed by Madho Dasa: Mahaprabhu has stayed in the 'Odia kingdom' and 'taken to observing Odia practices'. Cf. 3.105 and 3.58 ('the Odia brahmin'). The episode of the letter (3.129–3.139) repeats 3.76–3.86: once again Mahaprabhu sends a letter with a shloka to those who left.
  32. A shloka in the shardula-vikridita metre (four lines). Source not found. The second line is poorly read. Printed ଗଙ୍ଗାଦ୍ୱାରମଦର୍ଶୀ ନେକପଦବୀନାସ୍ଥାମଯୋଧ୍ୟା ପୁରଂ. The metre requires a short ି in adarśi ('[by me] was seen'), but ୀ is printed. ନେକପଦବୀ is taken as naika-padavī, 'many roads'. The sign after ନା resembles ସ୍ଥା or ରା; nāsthām (= na āsthām, 'no attachment'?) is only a guess. In the third line ମୁରରିପୁମୂର୍ତ୍ତିଂ is printed; the metre requires mura-ripor mūrtiṁ, 'the form of the Foe of Mura' (Krishna). Kutrāpi: ତ୍ର is printed with a tail below. 3.133–3.139 are the Odia paraphrase of the letter. Gangadvara is Haridvar; 'the confluence of the Ganga' is evidently Prayaga (or Ganga-sagara); 'the town of cowherds' is probably Gokula. According to CC (Madhya 17–19), Mahaprabhu visited Kashi, Prayaga, Mathura and Vrindavana. According to CC, He did not go to Dvaraka, Ayodhya or Badarikashrama. The words 'I have seen' here may refer to the pilgrimages of those same Vaishnavas (3.120).
  33. Nila-kandara ('the Blue Cave') is a name of Puri, like Nilachala ('the Blue Mountain'). 3.136–3.137 give an Odia teaching: Krishna left the former places of His pastimes at the end of the yuga and now abides in Puri as Jagannatha. Gaudiya Vaishnavas worship Jagannatha as Krishna Himself. Mahaprabhu saw Krishna in Him and longed to take Him to Vrindavana (CC, Madhya 13). But they hold Krishna's pastimes in Vrindavana to be eternal, and Vrindavana to be the highest abode, which Krishna never leaves (CC, Adi 5).
  34. 3.141–3.142 are understood tentatively. Nebe sehi is 'He will take' or 'that one will take', and puruṣottame is 'to Purushottama' or 'in Purushottama'. The sense adopted: the Vaishnavas hoped that Mahaprabhu would abolish the title 'Atibada' for their sake and bring them back to Puri. The letter, however, only repeats that He will not leave Jagannatha. Hence the decision of 3.143–3.144.
  35. From 3.145 the author speaks. According to Divakara, the Gaudiyas, offended with Puri, go to Vrindavana. There they 'reject' the injunctions of the Vedas and Puranas and the customs of Purushottama (3.145–3.148). According to CC, Mahaprabhu Himself sent Rupa and Sanatana Gosvami to Vrindavana to uncover the lost places of Krishna's pastimes and to write books on bhakti (CC, Madhya 19, 23; Antya 4). Gaudiya Vaishnavas, following Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati, hold their teaching to be grounded in shastra. Their guides are the Hari-bhakti-vilasa of Sanatana and Gopala Bhatta and the works of the Gosvamis.
  36. The dispute over the beginning of the mahamantra: 'Hare Rama…' (the Odia custom) or 'Hare Krishna…' (the Gaudiyas). Cf. VL 6.1–6.18 and the note to VL 6.15: there Mahaprabhu Himself decides that in Nilachala the mantra begins with 'Hare Rama' and in Gauda with 'Hare Krishna'. In Divakara the Gaudiyas abandon the order of Purushottama on their own. On the 'sixteen [names]' see the note to 2.160. Gaudiya Vaishnavas, following Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati, chant the mahamantra beginning with 'Hare Krishna'.
  37. Nirmalya is the dried mahaprasad of Jagannatha, and also the flowers and other items offered to the Deity. In Puri it is honoured and sent out with pilgrims. Divakara's charge differs from CC: there Mahaprabhu and His Gaudiya associates receive Jagannatha's mahaprasad with reverence (CC, Madhya 12; Antya 16). ଭଜିଲେ (?): printed ଭ + a sign ଜ or ବ + ଲେ, with ି not visible. ରଜ is taken as 'dust' (raja). 'Vraja' may also be meant.
  38. Madana-mohana ('He who enchants even Cupid') is Krishna, the Deity of Sanatana Gosvami in Vrindavana. Gaudiya Vaishnavas honour Madana-mohana, Govinda and Gopinatha as the principal Deities of Vrindavana, installed by the Gosvamis. The 'abandoning' of Jagannatha's form is Divakara's accusation. According to the CC, the Gaudiyas worshipped Jagannatha as Krishna Himself (see the note to 3.137).
  39. On the 'Hari-mandira' tilaka see the note to 2.150. The second half-line is read with doubt. କଳା (?) is printed as କ + ଲା; understood as kaḷā, 'black'. Kalā is also possible. The last word is printed as flagged ଅ + a sign like ସ୍ୱ (= ରା) + ଧ + ଲେ; understood as ଆରାଧିଲେ, 'they honoured'. It may be ଆଦରିଲେ, 'they adopted with regard'. Which tilaka Divakara calls 'black' is unclear. Gaudiya Vaishnavas wear the same urdhva-pundra (the 'temple of Hari'), of gopi-chandana or Vraja clay (Hari-bhakti-vilasa, ch. 4). The charge of abandoning the 'Hari-mandira' is the author's view.
  40. Baidha karma is service by the rules of scripture (vaidhi-bhakti); rāga-mārga is the path of spontaneous love (raganuga-bhakti). According to the CC (Madhya 22) and Rupa Gosvami's Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu (1.2), Mahaprabhu Himself taught both paths. Raganuga-bhakti follows the example of the eternal residents of Vraja but does not reject scripture. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati warned against imitating raga without purity of heart. He did not approve of abandoning the rules: the Gosvamis themselves compiled the Hari-bhakti-vilasa on vaidhi-bhakti. Divakara, however, presents the Gaudiyas as rejecting the rules (cf. 3.145).
  41. 3.154–3.157 give the Gaudiyas' reasoning as Divakara reports it: the Lord is subject to the devotee's feeling; where devotees dwell, there is Purushottama. Cf. the well-known verse ascribed to the Padma Purana: 'I abide where My devotees sing.' This argument answers 3.60–3.66, where Mahaprabhu glorifies the Purushottama-kshetra. In 3.178–3.182 Divakara apparently grants the first half of the argument: the Lord 'is found there' where devotees speak of Him. ଭବେ (3.156) is printed without ା; understood as ଭାବେ, 'by feeling', as in the second half-line.
  42. Govardhana Hill, the Yamuna and the kadamba trees are places of Krishna's pastimes in Vraja. The parikrama of Vraja is the circuit of its holy places. According to the CC (Madhya 17–18), Mahaprabhu Himself went round Vrindavana, Govardhana and the forests of Vraja. Here this is described as the doing of the Gaudiyas who turned away from Purushottama.
  43. The 'six Gosains' (ṣaṛa gosāi̐) are the six Gosvamis of Vrindavana. Their list is given in 3.170–3.172 (see the note to 3.170). Emantare is understood as 'thus'; possibly 'meanwhile'.
  44. Mathura Dasa is not identified; no such companion appears in the CC/CB. The reading ଚାଇଣ (3.162) is tentative: printed a sign like ସ୍ୱ + ଇଣ (cf. ଚାହିଁ in 3.91, 3.106). 3.163b literally reads 'you will bring Mathura Dasa'. It is understood thus: -ku here marks the addressee — '[He said] to Mathura Dasa' (cf. 'they said, looking at Chaitanya', 3.106) — and those to be brought are the Gosvamis (3.165–3.166). According to the CC, Mahaprabhu Himself sent Rupa and Sanatana to Vrindavana (Madhya 19, 23). They came to Puri separately, not at a summons: Rupa through Bengal (Antya 1), Sanatana through the Jharikhanda forest at the time of the Ratha-yatra (Antya 4; cf. VL 5.40, 5.73–5.76).
  45. The Gundicha-yatra is the Ratha-yatra: the Deities ride on chariots to the Gundicha temple (cf. the note to VL 5.75). According to the CC (Madhya 14), when Jagannatha's chariot stopped and the elephants could not move it, Mahaprabhu pushed it with His head, and the chariot moved. ସଙ୍ଗତୁଲେ (3.166) is read tentatively: printed ସଙ୍ଗ + a ligature like ଭୁ or ତୁ, + ଲେ (cf. ତୁଲେ, 'together with', 3.73). 'Twenty persons' (koṛie mūrtti): cf. 'six persons' in 3.73.
  46. The syntax of 3.170–3.172 is uncertain. 3.170b literally reads 'Sri Sanatana's joy' (or 'Sri Sanatana — joy'). Yeu̐ gosāi̐ means 'who [is] Gosain'. Divakara's six are Nityananda, Sanatana, Rupa, Raghunatha Dasa, Jiva and Gopala Dasa. Gaudiya Vaishnavas name as the six Gosvamis Rupa, Sanatana, Raghunatha Bhatta, Raghunatha Dasa, Jiva and Gopala Bhatta. Nityananda is not among them: according to the CC (Madhya 15) and CB (Antya 5), Mahaprabhu sent Him to preach in Gauda. Divakara lacks Raghunatha Bhatta; 'Gopala Dasa' is presumably Gopala Bhatta. Jiva Gosvami, the nephew of Rupa and Sanatana, came to Vrindavana, by Gaudiya tradition, only after Mahaprabhu's disappearance. ମୋକ୍ଷ (3.173) is printed clearly; it may be a misprint for ମୁଖ୍ୟ, 'chief'.
  47. 3.174–3.176: the Gosvamis come every year to the Gundicha and return to Vrindavana. According to the CC, it was the Gaudiyas from Bengal who came every year for the Ratha-yatra (Madhya 16; Antya 10, 12; see the note to 3.71). The Gosvamis from Vrindavana, by the CC, came to Puri only once each — Rupa (Antya 1) and Sanatana (Antya 4).
  48. 3.177–3.183 give the author's explanation: the Gaudiyas did not value Mahaprabhu's honour because they were close to Him. Examples of such closeness follow. Bhrigu struck Vishnu on the chest with his foot (Bhagavata 10.89); tradition links this blow with a mark on Vishnu's chest (here the Srivatsa). Nanda beats Krishna, seizing Him by the tuft: in the Bhagavata it is Yashoda who punishes Krishna (10.9). In their games the cowherd boys leap onto Krishna's shoulders (10.18). Gaudiya Vaishnavas see in such closeness the higher rasas of sakhya and vatsalya, free from reverential awe (CC, Adi 4). With Divakara it serves as a reproach.
  49. The word କମ୍ପା (??) is unclear: printed କ + ମ with a subscript resembling ପ or ଭ, + ା. Understood as kampa, 'trembling', i.e. reverential fear. The translation is tentative.
  50. 3.184 sums up the chapter: the Gaudiyas finally went to Vrindavana because of the title 'Atibada'. ନେଉଟି is understood as leuṭi, 'returning' (cf. ଲେଉଟି 3.116). Mahaprabhu, however, remains in Puri with Jagannatha. On the Gaudiya Vaishnava position see the notes to 3.44 and 3.79. According to the CC, the Gaudiyas did not leave Mahaprabhu; the Gosvamis lived in Vrindavana by His order.
  51. On the order of the mahamantra ('Hare Rama Krishna' among the Odias, 'Hare Krishna Rama' among the Gaudiyas) see the note to 3.147. According to Divakara, Mahaprabhu Himself chants it in the Odia order.
  52. The colophon is set in two lines, as at the end of Chapters 1 and 2 (see the note to the colophon of Ch. 2). Chapter 3 is also called 'Anukramani'; printed ଅନୁକର୍ମଣି, understood as ଅନୁକ୍ରମଣି. After Jagannatha's name there is here neither 'Dasa' (Ch. 1) nor 'Gosain' (Ch. 2): 'Sri Atibada Jagannatha'. The avagraha in ତୃତୀୟୋଽଧ୍ୟାୟଃ is printed like ୧. 3.187–3.188 are the author's signature (bhanita).
